examples.en: The child broke a cup.
I'm sorry I broke the plate.
You must not break the window. Be careful.
My younger sibling broke the glass window with a ball.
Some shell got in when I cracked the egg.
They broke the ice and caught fish.

explain: '깨다'는 '컵을 깨다'처럼 목적어가 있고, 깨는 사람이 있어요. 저절로 깨졌다면 '컵이 깨졌어요'처럼 '깨지다'를 써요. '약속을 깨다, 기록을 깨다, 분위기를 깨다'처럼 비유로도 많이 써요. 잠에서 '깨다'와 글자와 활용('깨요')이 같아서 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.example: 제가 괜히 분위기를 깬 것 같아서 미안해요.
phrases.en: I'm sorry, I feel like I ruined the mood for no reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 즐겁던 자리를 갑자기 어색하게 만들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone suddenly makes an enjoyable gathering awkward.

explain_en: '깨다' takes an object and has someone doing the breaking, as in '컵을 깨다'. When something breaks by itself, use '깨지다', as in '컵이 깨졌어요'. It is also used figuratively, as in 약속을 깨다, 기록을 깨다 and 분위기를 깨다. It is spelled and conjugated like 깨다 (to wake up), so context decides.

examples.en: There is warm rice on the table.
Mother is setting the table.
The table is full of side dishes.

examples.ko: 다 먹었으면 상 좀 치워 줄래요?
examples.en: If you're done eating, could you clear the table?

examples.ko: 이 상은 다리를 접을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can fold the legs of this table.

examples.ko: 손님이 오셔서 상이 하나 더 필요해요.
examples.en: Guests have come, so we need one more table.

explain: 바닥에 앉아서 밥을 먹는 낮은 '상'이에요. '상을 차리다', '상을 치우다'가 자주 쓰는 짝말이고, 식사용은 '밥상'이라고도 해요. 의자에 앉아 쓰는 '식탁'이나 공부하는 '책상'과 달라요. 상(prize)과 글자가 같아서 '차리다, 치우다'가 오면 table이에요.

phrases.en: On holidays, we lay out so much food that the table legs almost bend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 아주 푸짐하게 차려졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a huge, generous spread of food has been set out.

explain_en: It is the low table you sit at on the floor to eat. '상을 차리다' (set the table) and '상을 치우다' (clear the table) are the usual pairings, and a table for meals is also called '밥상'. It differs from '식탁', where you sit on chairs, and from '책상' (desk). It is spelled like 상 (prize), so with 차리다 or 치우다 it means table.

examples.en: My surname is Park and my first name is Jimin.

examples.ko: 한국 사람은 성이 한 글자인 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Many Korean people have a one-syllable surname.
People don't change their surname even when they marry.
In Korea, the surname and first name are written together.

examples.ko: 성만 같고 서로 전혀 모르는 사이예요.
examples.en: They only share a surname and don't know each other at all.
Both the surname and the first name are really unusual.

explain: 한국에서는 성이 이름 앞에 오고 띄어 쓰지 않아서 '김민수'처럼 써요. 다른 사람의 이름을 높여 물을 때는 '성함이 어떻게 되세요?'라고 해요. '성'은 '성씨'라고도 해요. 성(castle)과 글자가 같아서 이름 이야기면 surname이에요.

phrases.en: Write your surname and given name separately on the application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류에서 성과 이름을 나누어 적을 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a form asks for the surname and given name separately.

explain_en: In Korea the surname comes before the first name and is written without a space, as in '김민수'. To politely ask someone's name, you say '성함이 어떻게 되세요?'. '성' is also called '성씨'. It is spelled like 성 (castle), so in name talk it means surname.

examples.en: The priest is at the church you can see over there.
I met the priest at the local church yesterday.
I told the priest about my worries.
Today the priest also had lunch with us.
The new priest speaks Korean well.

examples.ko: 신부님과 함께 성당 앞에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo in front of the church with the priest.

explain: 가톨릭 사제는 보통 '신부님'처럼 '님'을 붙여 불러요. 개신교는 '목사님', 불교는 '스님'이라고 해서 종교마다 부르는 말이 달라요. 같은 소리의 '신부'(bride)는 '신랑'과 짝이니 문장 속에서 구별하세요.

phrases.en: The priest at the church holds Mass every Sunday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가톨릭 사제를 높여서 부르거나 말할 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a respectful way to address or refer to a Catholic priest.

explain_en: A Catholic priest is usually addressed with '님', as in '신부님'. Protestants say '목사님' and Buddhists say '스님', so the title differs by religion. The same-sounding '신부' (bride) pairs with '신랑', so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: A bee is sitting on the flower.
I got stung by a bee in the mountains and my arm swelled up.

examples.ko: 벌은 여러 꽃을 날아다니며 꿀을 모아요.
examples.en: Bees fly from flower to flower collecting honey.
A bee flew in through the window.
In spring, lots of bees fly around the garden.
The grandfather who keeps bees gave me some honey.

explain: 꿀을 모으는 벌은 '꿀벌', 더 큰 벌은 '말벌'이라고 해요. 벌에게 물렸을 때는 '벌에 쏘이다'라고 말해요. 같은 소리의 '벌'(punishment)과는 앞뒤 말로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: I got stung by a bee on the mountain and it hurt a lot.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a bee stings someone.

explain_en: The honey-making bee is a '꿀벌', and the larger kind is a '말벌'. When you get stung, you say '벌에 쏘이다'. Tell it apart from the same-sounding '벌' (punishment) by the surrounding words.

examples.en: I was punished because I didn't do my homework.
The teacher made us clean the classroom as a punishment.
What kind of penalty is there if you are late for class?

examples.ko: 이번 벌은 너무 심하지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this punishment isn't too harsh.

examples.ko: 잘못한 아이에게는 벌도 필요하지만 설명도 필요해요.
examples.en: A child who did wrong needs punishment, but also needs an explanation.

examples.ko: 그 벌 때문에 일주일 동안 밖에 못 나갔어요.
examples.en: Because of that punishment, I couldn't go out for a week.

explain: 반대말은 '상'이고, '벌을 받다 / 벌을 주다 / 벌을 서다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사가 정해져 있어요. 규칙을 어겨서 내는 돈은 '벌금'이에요. 소리가 같은 '벌'(bee)과는 문장 속에서 구별해요.

phrases.example: 숙제를 안 해서 복도에서 벌을 섰어요.
phrases.en: I didn't do my homework, so I was made to stand in the hallway as punishment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못해서 선 채로 처벌을 받을 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is made to stand as a punishment for misbehaving.
phrases.en_equiv: be made to stand as punishment

explain_en: The opposite is '상' (reward), and it pairs with fixed verbs such as '벌을 받다', '벌을 주다' and '벌을 서다'. Money paid for breaking a rule is a '벌금' (fine). Tell it apart from the same-sounding '벌' (bee) by context.
